hudson-valley.overview: The Hudson Valley has a vast network of day hikes, from steep scrambles in the Hudson Highlands to the carriage roads and cliff-edge trails of the Shawangunks. Many trailheads are accessible by a short drive or a direct train from New York City. The hiking ranges from easy forest loops to steep rock scrambles like Breakneck Ridge, rewarding hikers with sweeping views of the river and the Catskill foothills.

months.7: July is hot and humid, so hikers should start early in the day to explore the valley paths before the midday heat sets in.
months.10: October offers some of the best hiking of the year, with crisp air and clear views from the tops of the karst formations.

texas-hill-country.overview: The Texas Hill Country features modest but scenic day hikes through limestone canyons, oak woodlands, and river valleys. The standout route is the short, steep walk up the pink granite dome of Enchanted Rock, which needs a reservation on weekends and holidays. Trails are mostly short and gentle, with the best hiking found in the region's state parks.

sydney.overview: Sydney has coastal paths and nearby mountain trails accessible by train or a short drive. The walking ranges from easy harbor routes to the 16-mile Coast Track in Royal National Park, usually split over two days. Inland, the Blue Mountains provide dramatic sandstone cliffs and deep valleys, with popular day hikes like the Grand Canyon track and the Three Sisters walk.

okinawa.overview: Okinawa features modest but rewarding day hikes, mostly in the subtropical Yanbaru forest in the north and on coastal paths. Trails are short, from easy boardwalks to the muddy old logging road up Yonaha-dake, the island's highest peak, where hikers turn back at the ninth station marker. Winter is best, avoiding summer heat and typhoons.

queenstown.overview: Queenstown is a base for exploring the Southern Alps on foot, offering everything from steep day hikes to multi-day alpine routes. The long, steep hike up Ben Lomond begins with a gondola ride to skip the lower slopes, rewarding hikers with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the surrounding peaks. Trekkers come for the Routeburn Track, a 20-mile alpine crossing, and the Kepler Track, both requiring advance hut bookings. The best conditions run from December through March, when the high passes are clear of snow.

months.6: Deep snow covers the mountains, shifting the focus away from high-elevation hiking. Hikers can still enjoy crisp, clear days on the lower valley trails and lakeside paths, though the major alpine routes are impassable without mountaineering gear.
months.9: Temperatures slowly rise, but the alpine routes remain buried under deep snow. Hikers stick to the valley floors and lower hillsides, where the paths are clear and offer great views of the frozen peaks above.

months.5: The Fish River Canyon trek opens on the first of the month, kicking off the prime walking window. Hikers can tackle the 53-mile route through the gorge, while day hikers enjoy clear, cool mornings on the Sossusvlei dunes.

marlborough-abel-tasman.overview: This region is famous for coastal walking, anchored by the Abel Tasman Coast Track, a 37-mile, multi-day Great Walk through native forest and along golden-sand bays. The 44-mile Queen Charlotte Track features a similar mix of bush and coastal views in the Marlborough Sounds. Both routes are often accessed by water taxi, allowing hikers to hike a single section as a day trip. Because this is one of New Zealand's sunniest regions and the trails stay near sea level, the walking remains open year-round.

months.6: June is cool and can be damp, but the Abel Tasman Coast Track and Queen Charlotte Track stay open. Hikers should be prepared for shorter daylight hours and cooler temperatures.

mauritius.overview: Mauritius features solid day hiking anchored by Black River Gorges National Park and the dramatic Le Morne Brabant peninsula. Hikers can explore the forested trails to Black River Peak or tackle the steep, rocky scramble up Le Morne for sweeping views of the Indian Ocean. The best conditions run from May to October, avoiding the heavy rains that make the steep rock routes dangerous.

lapland.overview: Finnish Lapland has vast forests and rolling fells for hikers seeking remote wilderness. The region is famous for multi-day hut-to-hut routes like the 31-mile Hetta-Pallas trail and the 50-mile Karhunkierros trek, alongside shorter day hikes to open summits. The hiking season is short, peaking in early autumn when the fells turn red and gold.

months.3: The snowpack remains deep across the region. Hikers use snowshoes to explore the taiga or stick to short, groomed winter paths around the villages.
months.11: Daylight fades fast and the first deep snow settles. Hikers use snowshoes or stay on short, groomed paths around the villages.
months.12: Snow piles up in near-continuous darkness. Hikers stay on snowshoe tracks and short groomed paths around the villages.

peru.overview: Cusco and the Sacred Valley feature famous trekking, leading through the high Andes to ancient ruins. The multi-day routes are the main draw, led by the four-day Inca Trail to Machu Picchu, which needs a permit booked months ahead, and the demanding, high-altitude Salkantay trek past glacier-capped peaks. Day hikers can tackle the steep climb to Rainbow Mountain at over 16,000 feet, or explore shorter paths between Inca sites. The best conditions run from May to September, while heavy rains disrupt routes early in the year.

tierra-del-fuego.overview: Walking at the end of the world means rugged trails through southern beech forests, peat bogs, and jagged peaks overlooking the Beagle Channel. Tierra del Fuego National Park delivers accessible day hikes to coastal bays and glacier-fed lakes. For serious trekkers, a flight to Isla Navarino reaches the Dientes de Navarino circuit, a demanding multi-day route through remote, wind-battered alpine terrain.

months.3: Temperatures begin to drop and the first dustings of snow can appear on the heights. The Dientes de Navarino trek is still viable, but hikers should be prepared for colder, more unpredictable weather.

punta-cana.overview: The Dominican Republic has the highest mountain trekking in the Caribbean, centered on the demanding multi-day route up Pico Duarte. Hikers can also explore the cloud forests of Valle Nuevo National Park and the coastal trails of the Samaná Peninsula. The best conditions for the high-altitude treks and inland day hikes run from December to April, avoiding the heavy rains and intense heat of the hurricane season.

puerto-rico.overview: Puerto Rico features lush tropical day hikes, anchored by the dense rainforest trails of El Yunque and the steep, forested paths of the Cordillera Central. Hikers navigate muddy tracks to reach hidden waterfalls, observation towers, and sweeping views of the Caribbean coast.

turks-caicos.overview: Turks and Caicos features a few modest coastal walks for visitors looking to explore beyond the beaches. The best known is the Crossing Place Trail on Middle Caicos, which follows coastal cliffs, while Providenciales has the short Bird Rock Trail.

taiwan.overview: Taiwan's hiking runs from the marble walls of Taroko Gorge to the high-altitude trails of the Central Mountain Range. The main route is the demanding ascent of Yushan, a two-day trek to a 12,970-foot summit that requires a lottery permit. Day hikers can tackle the exposed Zhuilu Old Road cliff path in Taroko, which also needs a permit, or ride the forest railway to Alishan for walks among ancient cypress trees. October and November bring the clearest skies and most comfortable temperatures for the trails.

months.5: The plum rain season arrives, bringing heavy, persistent showers that make trails muddy and obscure the mountain views. Hikers should stick to paved or well-graded paths in the lower forests.
months.12: Temperatures drop sharply in the mountains, and the first snows often dust the highest summits. Northern trails return to a drizzly pattern, pushing the best hiking to the southern and central lower elevations.

months.1: Deep snow covers the park, closing the high alpine routes. Hikers can snowshoe or use winter traction on the lower valley trails around Bear Lake.
months.11: Snow settles across the park, ending the standard hiking season. Hikers shift to snowshoes or winter traction on the lower valley trails.

zion-bryce.overview: Zion and Bryce Canyon feature dramatic desert day hiking. In Zion, the exposed Angels Landing trail climbs a narrow sandstone fin (permit required), while the Narrows involves wading directly up the Virgin River through a slot canyon. Bryce Canyon provides a completely different landscape, with trails like the Navajo Loop descending into an amphitheater of bright orange hoodoos. Spring and fall bring the best weather, avoiding the extreme summer heat of Zion's canyon floor and the winter snows of Bryce's high rim.

zimbabwe.overview: Walking here means guided walking safaris in the bush and easy, scenic strolls along the Zambezi River. Mana Pools and Hwange have guided walks where visitors track wildlife on foot through the savanna. Around Victoria Falls, paved paths trace the gorge edge for views of the plunging water. Because of dangerous wildlife, all bush walks require an armed guide, and the best routes operate only during the dry months.

yosemite.overview: Yosemite has granite and waterfall hiking in a class of its own. The valley features the steep Mist Trail to Vernal and Nevada Falls, while the famous Half Dome cables require a lottery permit and a big day of climbing. High-country trails off Tioga Road lead to alpine lakes and sweeping domes. The best access runs from June to October when the high passes are clear of snow.

months.2: Winter conditions keep the high country closed. Hikers in the valley can find snow-dusted paths and snowshoe routes, but higher trails are inaccessible.

yellowstone.overview: Yellowstone features a vast network of trails ranging from geyser basin boardwalks to deep wilderness routes. Day hikers can climb to the Grand Prismatic overlook via the Fairy Falls trail or explore the rim of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone. Backcountry routes deliver multi-day treks through remote valleys, though hikers must carry bear spray and stay alert for wildlife.

months.12: Winter snow settles in across the park. Hikers stick to snowshoe routes and groomed trails near the geyser basins.

whistler.overview: Vancouver and Whistler have mountain hiking, from coastal rainforests to the high alpine of Garibaldi Provincial Park. Day hikers can tackle steep ascents to glacier-fed lakes and panoramic ridges, or explore lower valley loops. The best alpine routes, like the trails to Garibaldi Lake and Joffre Lakes, require free day passes in summer. The high country is strictly a summer destination, with snow burying the peaks for much of the year.

vietnam.overview: Vietnam's best hiking is in the northern highlands, where trails link remote villages through terraced valleys and steep limestone peaks. The main draws are multi-day homestay treks around Sapa and Ha Giang, and the demanding guided climb up Fansipan. The season is driven by the monsoon, with heavy summer rains turning trails to deep mud.

vienna.overview: Vienna features accessible day hiking in the Vienna Woods, a forested ridge easily reached by train or tram. Hikers can take on easy trails up Kahlenberg for views over the city and the Danube, or explore the shaded paths of the Hagenbachklamm gorge.

vermont.overview: Vermont delivers classic New England hiking through the dense forests of the Green Mountains. The main route is the Long Trail, a rugged 273-mile trek spanning the state, while day hikers tackle the steep, rocky ascents of Mount Mansfield and Camel's Hump for sweeping views over the valleys. Lower elevations provide gentler loops through maple and birch woods.

uzbekistan.overview: Uzbekistan's best hiking lies away from its famous Silk Road cities, up in the Western Tian Shan and the Nuratau mountains. Day hikers head to the Chimgan area near Tashkent, where routes range from the loop over Little Chimgan to the steep, rocky ascent of Greater Chimgan. The scenery shifts from arid foothills to alpine meadows and rugged ridges. Spring and fall bring the best weather for the lower ranges.

upper-peninsula.overview: The Upper Peninsula's hiking is defined by the rugged Lake Superior shoreline and deep northern forests. The main draws are the cliff-top trails at Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore and the old-growth forest paths of the Porcupine Mountains. Isle Royale National Park, reached only by ferry or seaplane, provides a remote wilderness trek. The season is short, driven by heavy winter snows and muddy spring thaws.

uluru.overview: Walking gives a sense of the scale of the Red Centre's sandstone formations. The main routes are day hikes, including the flat loop around the base of Uluru, the rocky Valley of the Winds trail through the domes of Kata Tjuta, and the steep climb to the Kings Canyon rim. The desert environment dictates the hiking schedule, with extreme heat forcing early starts and trail closures during the hottest months.

months.7: The coolest month of the year offers the safest and most comfortable hiking. The Valley of the Winds trail remains open all day, allowing hikers to fully explore the deep gorges of Kata Tjuta.

uganda.overview: Uganda has serious equatorial trekking in the Rwenzori Mountains, known as the Mountains of the Moon, and on Mount Elgon. The Rwenzori Central Circuit is a strenuous multi-day trek through giant lobelias and alpine bogs, which requires a guide. Shorter day hikes explore the dense forests around Bwindi and Kibale, where the trails are often steep and muddy.

tuscany.overview: Tuscany's walking winds through rolling landscapes, vineyards, and historic hill towns. The multi-day Via Francigena pilgrim route connects Lucca to Siena, while day hikers can explore the Val d'Orcia or the nearby Cinque Terre coastal paths in Liguria. Spring and fall provide the best weather for these exposed routes.

tbilisi-caucasus.overview: The Georgian Caucasus delivers spectacular mountain hiking, from day hikes to remote glaciers to multi-day village routes. The famous four-day, 34-mile trek from Mestia to Ushguli in Svaneti connects ancient stone towers via guesthouse stays. Day hikers heading north from Tbilisi can tackle the steep 3.7-mile round trip to the Gergeti Trinity Church, or push further on the long 12-mile round trip to the Gergeti Glacier. The high mountain routes are fully open from July through September.

tasmania.overview: Tasmania has dramatic hiking, from the dolerite peaks of Cradle Mountain to the white sands of Freycinet. The island is famous for the Overland Track, a six-day, 40-mile alpine trek through the central highlands that needs an advance booking from October to May. Day hikers can tackle the steep, rocky ascent of Cradle Mountain or the coastal trails above Wineglass Bay. The best conditions run from December to February, while the middle of the year brings snow and harsh weather to the highlands.

months.7: July is cold and wet, with deep snow often covering the alpine routes, though coastal trails remain open for hardy hikers.
months.10: October marks the reopening of the Overland Track booking season, with hikers returning to the highlands despite lingering chill.

tanzania.overview: Northern Tanzania's hiking centers on Mount Kilimanjaro, an expedition trek that takes hikers to the roof of Africa without technical climbing gear. Multi-day routes like the Machame, Lemosho, and the hut-to-hut Marangu trail climb through rainforest and alpine desert to a glaciated summit. Beyond the big peak, visitors can take on the steep multi-day trek up Mount Meru or walk the forested rim of the Ngorongoro Crater. All Kilimanjaro and Meru routes require mandatory registered guides and park fees.

svalbard.overview: Hiking in Svalbard means guided day walks across open tundra and glaciers, often reached by boat from Longyearbyen. Because of polar bears, anyone leaving the settlement must carry a means of scaring them off, and most hikers go with an armed guide. The short summer window features stark Arctic scenery, from steep climbs up local peaks like Sarkofagen to remote shorelines.

months.6: Summer hiking begins as the tundra thaws, allowing boats to drop hikers at remote trailheads for guided day hikes.

srilanka.overview: Sri Lanka delivers lush hill country trails and striking rock fortress climbs. The most famous route is the night ascent of Adam's Peak, a steep climb up thousands of stairs to catch the sunrise, while day hikers head to the viewpoints of Ella Rock and Pidurangala. The best hiking aligns with the drier months from December to March.

southeast-alaska.overview: Hiking here means walking into deep coastal rainforests and up to glacier views, often starting right from the port towns. Juneau has the steep, unmaintained West Glacier Trail for a close look at the ice, while Skagway is the start of the Chilkoot Trail, a 33-mile, multi-day trek over the historic gold rush pass. The season is short, driven by snowmelt, with trails at their best from June to August.

snowdonia.overview: Walking in Wales centers on Snowdonia, with the rugged peaks of Snowdon, the Glyderau, and the Carneddau. Hikers can tackle the steep Watkin Path with its 3,300-foot climb to the summit of Snowdon, or take the classic Pyg and Miners' tracks past high mountain lakes.

months.1: Winter conditions grip the peaks, making the summits genuinely hazardous without an ice axe and crampons. Hikers stick to the lower valleys and sheltered forest trails.

singapore.overview: Singapore has modest but accessible walking, primarily on paved paths and elevated walkways. The main draw is the Southern Ridges, an easy trail connecting Mount Faber to Kent Ridge Park via the striking Henderson Waves bridge. Heat and humidity are constant year-round.

sicily.overview: Sicily delivers a mix of volcanic landscapes and coastal trails. The main draw is Mount Etna, where hikers can explore lower craters independently or hire a guide to reach the active summit zone when conditions allow. Elsewhere, the Zingaro Nature Reserve provides coastal paths above the Mediterranean, and the Madonie mountains have forested ridges. Spring and fall are the best times to walk, avoiding the intense summer heat.

months.1: Winter brings snow to Mount Etna, closing the higher trails to hikers, though snowshoeing is possible. Coastal paths like Zingaro remain open but can be cool and damp.

sequoia-kings-canyon.overview: Sequoia and Kings Canyon feature two distinct hiking worlds: the giant sequoia groves and the rugged High Sierra. Day hikers can walk among the massive trees on the Congress Trail or climb the granite dome of Moro Rock for panoramic views of the Great Western Divide. Trekkers come for multi-day routes like the 41.4-mile Rae Lakes Loop or the High Sierra Trail, which crosses the mountain range to Mount Whitney. The high alpine routes require wilderness permits and are only clear of snow from mid-summer to early fall.

seoul.overview: Seoul is a major city with real mountain hiking right on its subway lines. Bukhansan National Park delivers steep, rocky day hikes to granite peaks, with the steep climb to Baegundae rewarding hikers with views over the metropolis. Closer to the center, the Seoul City Wall traces the ridges of Bugaksan and Namsan on paved paths and stairs. The best hiking is in the clear, mild weather of spring and fall.

scottish-highlands-skye.overview: The Scottish Highlands and the Isle of Skye have dramatic hiking, defined by deep glens, rugged coastlines, and jagged peaks. Day hikers head to routes like the Quiraing landslip and the Old Man of Storr, where steep, rocky paths lead to sweeping views of the sea and moors. Multi-day hikers can tackle the 96-mile West Highland Way through the mainland valleys. Biting midges are notorious in the middle of the year.

months.1: Freezing temperatures, snow on the heights, and very short daylight hours limit options. High routes need winter skills, leaving hikers to low-level glen and coastal paths.
months.2: Cold, wet weather and short days keep hikers to low-level glens and coastal paths, with snow lingering on the high ground.
months.3: Daylight increases and lower trails begin to thaw, though snow and ice still cover the high ridges. Hikers stick to the glens and coastal routes.
months.10: Heavy rain, high winds, and rapidly shortening daylight make conditions tough. Hikers can still enjoy the glens, but high routes become muddy and exposed.

sardinia.overview: Sardinia features rugged Mediterranean hiking, from the deep limestone canyons of the Supramonte to the high peaks of the Gennargentu. Trails lead through wild macchia and ancient oak forests down to isolated coves like Cala Goloritzé. Spring and autumn provide the best weather for exploring the island's dramatic coastal cliffs and mountainous interior.

santorini.overview: Santorini's walking is defined by the famous caldera-rim path from Fira to Oia, a hilly route that traces the edge of the volcanic crater. The walking earns views of the Aegean Sea and the island's whitewashed villages that cannot be seen from the road. Beyond the rim, the island features modest coastal walks and paths through dry, terraced hills.

months.6: Summer heat builds quickly. The Fira to Oia path has very little shade, so hikers must start early in the morning to avoid the midday sun.
months.11: Cooler, less predictable weather arrives. The caldera path remains walkable, though hikers should be prepared for wind and occasional rain.

rwanda.overview: Rwanda has steep, muddy volcano climbs and dense forest trails that go with park guides. In Volcanoes National Park, hikers climb Mount Bisoke or Mount Karisimbi, or take the muddy trail to Dian Fossey's grave. Further south, Nyungwe National Park provides a network of trails through ancient montane rainforest.

rome.overview: Rome has modest but atmospheric walking just outside the urban center. The Via Appia Antica provides miles of easy, historic strolling past ancient ruins and umbrella pines. For more elevation, a short train ride reaches the Castelli Romani, where wooded trails loop around volcanic crater lakes like Lake Albano.

rioja.overview: Rioja has modest but scenic walking, blending agricultural landscapes with the rugged backdrop of the Sierra de Cantabria. Most routes are gentle to steady day hikes that start directly from the wine towns, leading through rolling vineyards and along the Ebro River. The best hiking is in spring and autumn, avoiding the intense summer heat and cold winters.

redwood.overview: Redwood National and State Parks have day hiking through ancient old-growth forests and along rugged Pacific coastlines. The signature routes wind beneath towering canopies, like the ten-mile James Irvine Trail or the easier walks in Prairie Creek. Walking here is a year-round pursuit, with dry summer months providing the clearest conditions and winter bringing heavy rain that turns the forest floor vibrant green.

months.2: Rain remains frequent, keeping the forest streams full and the fern-lined canyon walls dripping, though hikers should expect wet and muddy trails.
months.8: Late summer maintains ideal, dry trail conditions. Hikers can explore the towering groves and coastal bluffs comfortably, with Fern Canyon parking still requiring a reservation.
months.9: September brings some of the best hiking of the year, with warm, clear days and dry trails before the reservation requirement for Fern Canyon ends mid-month.

quebec-city.overview: Quebec City and Montreal feature accessible day hikes that trade deep wilderness for forested hills and glacial valleys just outside the urban centers. Near Quebec City, Parc national de la Jacques-Cartier provides steep climbs like the Les Loups trail, rewarding hikers with sweeping views of a deep river valley. Montreal's Mount Royal features easy, graded paths right in the city. The best hiking aligns with the vibrant fall foliage.

puglia.overview: Puglia has modest but scenic day hikes along the Adriatic and Ionian coasts. The best hiking is in the north on the Gargano Peninsula, where trails trace the limestone cliffs and loop through the ancient beech trees of the Foresta Umbra. Further south, the Salento peninsula features easy coastal paths above the sea.

provence.overview: Provence features day hiking, from the steep limestone inlets of the Calanques National Park on the Mediterranean coast to the trails connecting the hilltop villages of the Luberon. Routes range from easy coastal paths to long climbs up Mont Ventoux, with the best hiking found in the cooler shoulder seasons.

months.10: Autumn offers some of the best hiking conditions of the year, with mild air and clear views from the limestone ridges.

prague.overview: Prague has easy urban park walks and serves as a base for day trips to the dramatic landscapes of Bohemian Switzerland. About two hours away by train and bus, hikers can reach Pravcicka Gate, Europe's largest natural sandstone arch, and walk through deep forested gorges.

piedmont.overview: Piedmont has two distinct hiking landscapes: the rolling vineyard trails of the Langhe and the high alpine routes of Gran Paradiso National Park. Hikers can link wine villages on gentle loops around Barolo, with the Alps visible on clear days, or head north for long mountain day hikes and multi-day treks like the Grande Traversata delle Alpi.

months.2: The high mountains remain strictly snowbound. Hikers in the Langhe hills face chilly temperatures and dormant vineyards on the paths between wine towns.
months.10: Snow begins to close the high alpine passes. Hikers shift to the Langhe hills, where the trails offer spectacular autumn foliage and cool, foggy mornings.

paris.overview: Paris is a flat-city base for day walks by train: the vast Fontainebleau forest and sections of the GR11 loop. Walkers find gentle day hikes through ancient woodlands, sandstone ridges, and countryside. The city itself has flat urban park strolls.

papua-new-guinea.overview: Papua New Guinea is defined by the Kokoda Track, a grueling 60-mile, eight-day trek through dense jungle and steep, muddy ridges. Hikers come for the wartime history and the deep, remote wilderness of the Owen Stanley Range. Beyond Kokoda, the highland valleys feature shorter day hikes to remote villages and birding sites. The hiking is best from May to September when the trails are driest, as heavy rains turn the paths into deep mud for much of the rest of the year. A permit is required for the Kokoda Track.

panama.overview: Panama has tropical hiking ranging from the cloud forests of the western highlands to the lowland rainforests near the canal. The best-known routes center around Boquete, including the long hike up Volcán Barú for views that can stretch to both oceans on a clear day. Trails are often muddy and humid, with the dry season providing the most reliable conditions.

palawan.overview: Palawan is famous for its water, but short, steep trails reward hikers with sweeping views over the bays. The main walks are the 720 steps up Mount Tapyas in Coron and the steep scramble up Taraw Cliff in El Nido. These short day hikes are best tackled at dawn or dusk to avoid the heat, with the dry months from January to April offering the clearest skies.

pakistan.overview: Pakistan's Karakoram range delivers dramatic expedition trekking, dominated by the multi-week route up the Baltoro Glacier to K2 Base Camp. Shorter hikes reach the high pastures of Fairy Meadows beneath Nanga Parbat, while the Hunza Valley provides lower-elevation trails. The high-altitude routes require serious commitment, and the K2 trek mandates an approved guide and agency.

olympic.overview: Olympic National Park has three distinct hiking environments: glacier-capped alpine ridges, temperate rainforests, and rugged Pacific coastline. Hikers can tackle the long High Divide Loop for views of Mount Olympus, explore the moss-draped trails of the Hoh Rain Forest, or navigate the tidal zones of the Wilderness Coast on a multi-day trek. The best conditions run from July through September when the high trails melt out and the weather is reliably dry.

months.9: Excellent hiking continues with crisp air and clear skies. The high trails remain open and snow-free, providing some of the best hiking conditions of the year before the autumn rains arrive.

nyc.overview: Walking here means easy nature paths within the five boroughs: the wooded trails of Inwood Hill Park, the Staten Island Greenbelt and the paved loops of Central Park. All are reached by subway or ferry and give a break from the pavement, though they stay firmly urban.

nova-scotia.overview: Nova Scotia's best hiking traces the rugged Atlantic coastline and the highlands of Cape Breton. The famous Skyline Trail delivers a short, dramatic loop above the Gulf of St. Lawrence, where hikers often spot moose and whales from the headland boardwalks. Other day hikes along the Cabot Trail lead through deep river canyons and coastal forests.

months.6: Summer conditions settle in and the full trail network is open. The Skyline Trail offers clear views over the gulf, though hikers should prepare for occasional rain and early-season insects. From late in the month, parking at the Skyline Trail requires a timed reservation.
months.12: Snow begins to accumulate, closing the higher routes to standard hiking. Hikers turn to snowshoes for the lower valley paths as winter sets in.

months.4: Cooler air and shorter daylight hours arrive, but the main volcanic circuits remain open for hikers. Frost is common in the mornings, and hikers need to be prepared for rapidly changing weather on the exposed ridges.
months.5: Snow begins to accumulate on the higher elevations of Tongariro and Taranaki. The Great Walk season ends, meaning huts on the Northern Circuit drop their services, and hikers must check conditions carefully before heading up.
months.6: Deep snow and ice take over the high volcanic routes, turning the Tongariro Alpine Crossing into a technical objective that requires an ice axe and crampons. Hikers stick to the lower forest trails and coastal paths.
months.8: Heavy snowpack persists on the volcanic peaks, keeping the famous alpine crossings off-limits to standard hikers. Lower forest walks remain open, though hikers should expect cold temperatures and muddy sections.
months.9: Temperatures slowly begin to rise, but the high trails on Tongariro and Taranaki remain covered in snow and ice. Hikers continue to rely on the lower-elevation paths and coastal tracks.
months.10: The snow line gradually retreats, and the Great Walk season resumes on the Tongariro Northern Circuit. The high crossings may still hold patches of snow and ice, requiring hikers to check daily conditions before setting out.

north-cascades.overview: The North Cascades have dramatic alpine hiking, with steep trails leading to jagged peaks, deep valleys, and hanging glaciers. Day hikes like the long, steep climb up Sahale Arm or the shorter Cascade Pass deliver views of a vast, icy wilderness. The season is short, dictated by heavy winter snows that close the main highway for months, making late summer the only reliable window for the high country.

nice-riviera.overview: The French Riviera features modest but highly scenic coastal and hillside walking, easily reached by train or a short drive. The best known route is the steep Nietzsche Path climbing from the sea at Eze-sur-Mer up to the medieval village of Eze, while flatter coastal paths trace the rocky edges of Cap Ferrat and Cap d'Antibes.

months.8: August remains very hot, requiring hikers to start near dawn to comfortably handle the Nietzsche Path.
months.12: December provides crisp, cool days in the 50s, keeping the steep hillside trails open and pleasant for active hikers.

nicaragua.overview: Nicaragua delivers rugged day hikes focused on its volcanic peaks and cloud forests. The signature route is the steep, muddy climb up Volcán Maderas on Ometepe Island, usually done with a local guide, which rewards hikers with a crater lake and sweeping views of Lake Nicaragua. Other trails explore the slopes of active volcanoes and tropical reserves, with the best conditions falling between December and April.

napa.overview: Napa and Sonoma feature solid day hiking through oak woodlands, redwood groves, and chaparral-covered hills overlooking the vineyards. Trails in the local state parks climb steadily to ridgelines, rewarding hikers with sweeping views of the valleys and distant mountains. Spring brings vibrant green hills and wildflowers, while summer and early fall can be hot and dry.

morocco.overview: The High Atlas Mountains feature dramatic hiking within a few hours' reach of the city. The centerpiece is the two-day trek up Mount Toubkal, a 13,670-foot summit reached from the village of Imlil that rewards hikers with sweeping views over the rugged peaks and valleys. Lower trails wind through terraced Berber villages and walnut groves for long day hikes. The best conditions run from March to May and September to November, avoiding the intense mid-year heat and late-year snows.

months.1: Deep snow covers the high peaks, turning the Mount Toubkal route into a technical ascent requiring crampons and an ice axe. Hikers are limited to lower valley trails around Imlil.

monterey-big-sur.overview: Monterey and Big Sur deliver dramatic coastal hiking where trails trace ocean cliffs and drop into deep redwood canyons. Day hikers explore the rocky coves of Point Lobos State Natural Reserve and the steep, ocean-facing ridges of Garrapata State Park. Inland routes climb through shaded groves of old-growth coast redwoods in the Santa Lucia Mountains. The mild climate allows year-round hiking, though winter storms bring mud and road closures.

months.9: Fall brings some of the year's best hiking, with the summer fog lifting to reveal clear, expansive views over the Pacific.

mongolia.overview: Mongolia has vast steppes and rugged mountain terrain for adventurous hikers. Day hikers head to Gorkhi-Terelj National Park near Ulaanbaatar for rocky alpine scenery and valley routes, while remote multi-day treks explore the western Altai mountains. The short summer season is the only realistic window for walking here.

months.6: Summer offers the best hiking conditions, with clear trails in Gorkhi-Terelj and accessible multi-day routes in the western mountains.
months.12: Winter settles in with deep snow and extreme cold, keeping the trails closed to hikers.

milford-sound-fiordland.overview: Fiordland holds famous multi-day treks that lead hikers through glacier-carved valleys, dense rainforest, and alpine passes to the steep walls of the fjords. The Milford, Routeburn, and Kepler tracks are the main draws, requiring advance hut bookings in the Great Walks season. Day hikers can tackle sections of these routes or steep climbs like the Routeburn Shelter to Key Summit, earning views of the Darran Mountains and hanging valleys. The region is wet, so expect rain and waterfalls at any time of year.

months.5: The Great Walks season ends, and the huts are no longer serviced. Snow begins to accumulate on the higher passes, limiting hikers to lower-elevation day hikes and valley trails.
months.7: Deep snow and avalanche risk close the high routes entirely. Hikers are limited to short nature trails near the road or the lowest sections of the valleys, provided the Milford Road is open.
months.9: Snow begins to melt at lower elevations, but the alpine passes remain closed to hikers. Lower valley trails become more accessible, though conditions are often wet and muddy.
months.10: The Great Walks season begins late in the month as the huts reopen. The lower sections of the tracks are clear, but hikers may still encounter snow on the highest passes like the Routeburn's Harris Saddle.
months.12: Long daylight hours and warmer weather make this a prime month for the Milford, Routeburn, and Kepler tracks. The alpine scenery is fully accessible, though hikers should always be prepared for rain.

mendoza.overview: Mendoza is the gateway to the high Andes and Aconcagua Provincial Park, which requires an entry permit. Hikers drive in for long day hikes to viewpoints like Confluencia camp, or take multi-day treks toward the base camps of the highest peak outside Asia. High-altitude hiking runs mid-November to March, the Confluencia day hike stays open to the end of April, and lower trails in the Cordón del Plata can be hiked most of the year.

months.5: Deep snow closes the high-altitude routes in Aconcagua Provincial Park. Hikers are limited to the lower foothills and reserves, where the air is cold and the scenery is modest.
months.6: Deep snow closes the high Andes to hikers. Hiking is restricted to simple low-elevation walks in the foothills, in chilly weather.
months.8: The high mountains remain locked in snow. Hikers can explore the lower valleys and foothills, though the dramatic high-altitude routes are still out of reach.

maui.overview: Maui features two distinct hiking environments: the high-altitude volcanic landscape of Haleakalā and the lush rainforests of the coast. The standout route is the Sliding Sands Trail, which descends about 2,500 feet into the Haleakalā crater and requires a demanding climb back out to the rim at nearly 10,000 feet. On the wetter eastern side, the Pipiwai Trail leads through a dense bamboo forest to the towering Waimoku Falls.

mallorca.overview: Mallorca's Serra de Tramuntana mountains deliver rugged limestone peaks, deep gorges, and coastal views that drop straight into the Mediterranean. Day hikers can tackle the steep gorge scramble of the Torrent de Pareis or the panoramic Archduke's Trail, while the Dry Stone Route (GR221) provides a multi-day trek through olive groves and mountain refuges. The best hiking avoids the intense summer heat, focusing on the mild spring and fall.

maldives.overview: Walking here means short island loops and sandbank strolls rather than traditional trails. Visitors take a boat to reach stretches like the long sandbank at Dhigurah. The dry months from December to April bring the calmest conditions for exploring the islands on foot.

madagascar.overview: Madagascar has day hikes through deep sandstone canyons and limestone pinnacles. The best hiking is found in Isalo National Park, where mandatory guides lead hikers past gallery forests and natural pools, and in Andringitra for multi-day treks to Pic Boby. The dry months from April to November provide the most reliable trail access.

luangprabang.overview: Laos features rugged jungle trails and steep limestone viewpoint hikes, mostly in the northern mountains. The main draws are the day hikes around Nong Khiaw, where steep climbs lead to the Pha Daeng and Pha Noy viewpoints above the Nam Ou River and karst peaks, each taking a few hours in humid heat. Multi-day village-to-village treks also run through the northern forests, though heat and monsoon rains dictate when trails are passable.

los-cabos.overview: The region has some worthwhile desert and mountain trails away from the resorts. The best hiking is in the Sierra de la Laguna mountains, where long day hikes reach pine forests and sweeping views of the Baja peninsula. Closer to the coast, short desert paths explore canyons and scrubland. The season runs from late fall through early spring to avoid extreme heat.

london.overview: London offers modest but accessible walking, from the flat stretches of the Thames Path to the woodlands of Epping Forest. A short train ride reaches the North Downs, where routes like Box Hill provide a taste of the countryside.

lofoten.overview: The Lofoten Islands offer dramatic coastal hiking, with trails climbing steep granite ridges that drop directly into the Norwegian Sea. Hikers tackle challenging and sometimes technical day hikes that earn wide fjord and ocean panoramas, often under the midnight sun. The signature routes are short but relentlessly steep, like the stone staircase up Reinebringen or the rugged trail to the isolated sands of Kvalvika Beach. The best conditions run from late June through August.

months.2: Deep snow and ice keep the peaks closed to hikers as daylight slowly returns. Only short, flat coastal paths near the villages are practical, with microspikes or snowshoes.
months.10: The first snows dust the peaks and temperatures drop. High trails become icy and dangerous, pushing hikers back to the lower coastal routes.

lisbon.overview: Hiking around Lisbon means escaping the city for the forested hills of Sintra or the coastal ridges of Arrábida Natural Park. Trails range from easy paths between Sintra's palaces to day hikes along the Serra do Risco, offering views over the Atlantic Ocean. The best hiking happens in the mild spring and fall, avoiding the summer heat.

months.7: High temperatures make exposed coastal routes demanding; the shaded forests of Sintra offer the best hiking.

lake-district.overview: The Lake District is defined by steep, rugged fells and deep glacial valleys holding ribbon lakes. Hikers tackle steep ascents up Scafell Pike and Helvellyn, where high ridges like Striding Edge require a tolerance for heights and offer sweeping panoramas over the Cumbrian landscape. Lower elevations provide miles of graded paths around lakes like Derwentwater and Windermere. Multi-day hikers can cross the park on the 70-mile Cumbria Way.

months.2: Daylight begins to stretch, though the high ridges remain freezing and icy. Hikers stick to the lower, sheltered trails through the valleys and forests.
months.4: Longer days and drier trails make this a prime time to tackle the major peaks. The high ridges clear of ice, allowing hikers to safely navigate routes like Striding Edge.
months.7: The warmest temperatures of the year make high-altitude walking comfortable. Hikers can spend long days on the fells, though afternoon rain showers are always possible.
months.8: Late summer offers prime conditions for multi-day routes like the Cumbria Way. The high ridges are clear, though hikers should carry gear for sudden rain.
months.10: Heavy rain returns, turning the fellside trails slick and muddy. Hikers can still reach the summits, but low cloud often obscures the views.
months.11: Short daylight hours and dropping temperatures push hikers toward the lower valley loops. The high ridges see their first dustings of snow and ice.

ladakh.overview: Ladakh is a high-altitude desert of stark, jagged peaks and deep valleys, offering dramatic Himalayan trekking. The classic route is the Markha Valley trek, a multi-day journey crossing passes over 16,000 feet past remote villages and Buddhist monasteries. Day hikers can tackle steep acclimatization trails around Leh or explore the Sham Valley. The season is short, dictated by snow on the high passes, with the best hiking from June to September.

kerala.overview: Kerala's best hiking lies inland in the Western Ghats, where trails wind through tea estates, shola forests, and high-altitude grasslands. The main route is the long day hike up Meesapulimala near Munnar, which requires an advance permit and an authorized guide. The dry months bring the clearest views of the rolling green peaks, while the heavy summer monsoon brings leeches and washes out trails.

months.7: Torrential monsoon rains continue to wash out trails in the Ghats, keeping most hikers away.

kaziranga.overview: Northeast India's hiking runs through dense forests and rolling hills. The standout day hike descends thousands of steep stone steps to the living root bridges of Nongriat in Meghalaya. Further afield, the Dzukou Valley in Nagaland provides a lush, rolling trek, though visitors must secure the required permits for Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh before setting out.

months.1: Dry, cool weather makes this an ideal time to tackle the steep stone steps to the living root bridges or explore the Dzukou Valley, though mornings are often foggy.
months.12: Dry, cool air suits the long stone-step descents to Nongriat and the ridgelines of the Dzukou Valley, though morning fog is common.

seychelles.overview: Seychelles features modest but rewarding day hikes through tropical forests and over granite slabs. On Mahé, trails in Morne Seychellois National Park and the coastal path to Anse Major lead to secluded beaches and viewpoints. The walking is short and steep in places, best done in the drier, calmer months to avoid heavy rain and high humidity.

oaxaca.overview: The Sierra Norte mountains above Oaxaca hold the Pueblos Mancomunados, a network of Zapotec villages linked by more than 60 miles of trails. Hikers go point-to-point between the villages, staying in community-run cabins at elevations between 7,000 and 10,000 feet. The routes pass through pine-oak forests and cloud forests, offering a multi-day trek or day hikes that are easily reached from the city.

kenya.overview: While the main wildlife parks restrict independent walking, guided bush walks in the private Maasai Mara conservancies are a chance to experience the savanna on foot. Hell's Gate National Park allows unguided day hikes past geothermal vents and towering cliffs. For a serious multi-day expedition, the Sirimon and Naro Moru routes on Mount Kenya lead trekkers through alpine moorlands to the walk-up summit of Point Lenana at over 16,000 feet.

croatia.overview: The Dalmatian Coast landscape is defined by rugged karst mountains rising straight from the Adriatic, with the best hiking found in the limestone gorges of Paklenica National Park and the high ridges of Mount Biokovo. Inland, boardwalks weave through the waterfalls of Plitvice Lakes, a busy destination requiring timed tickets in summer. Most routes are day hikes ranging from easy coastal paths to steep, rocky ascents that demand sturdy footwear.

colombian-caribbean.overview: The famous multi-day route is the Ciudad Perdida, a hot, humid jungle trek of four to six days and roughly 30 miles through the Sierra Nevada foothills to ancient ruins, which requires an authorized guide. Day hikers flock to Tayrona National Park, where well-maintained and busy boardwalk trails transport tourists and locals through the coastal jungle to pristine boulder-strewn beaches. The dry months from December to April bring the best trail conditions.

chiang-mai.overview: Northern Thailand's best hiking is in Doi Inthanon National Park, home to Thailand's highest peak. There, the guided Kew Mae Pan nature trail is a short ridge loop near the summit road, with views over the Mae Pan valley, often above a sea of cloud. Doi Suthep, above Chiang Mai, has forest trails past Monthathan Waterfall. The best hiking is from November to January, when the air is clear and the Kew Mae Pan trail is open.

falklands.overview: The Falkland Islands have modest but scenic coastal walking across open, windswept ground. The Maritime History Trail runs from Stanley to Cape Pembroke, a short path leads to Magellanic penguins at Gypsy Cove, and a short flight reaches Sea Lion Island, where you can walk freely to wildlife colonies. The best window is October to March.

glacier-waterton.overview: Glacier and Waterton Lakes feature some of the most dramatic alpine hiking in North America, with trails carved into steep sedimentary rock above glacier-carved valleys. Hikers reach the best routes by driving the Going-to-the-Sun Road, taking park shuttles, or crossing lakes by boat. Long day hikes like the Highline Trail and Grinnell Glacier deliver views of jagged peaks and alpine lakes, while Waterton features the steep, cliff-hugging Crypt Lake trail. The high-country season is short, dictated by snowpack and road access.

months.1: Deep snow blankets the parks, closing the high country and the main scenic roads. Hikers can use snowshoes on lower valley routes near the park entrances, passing through snow-covered forests.
months.2: Deep snow blankets the parks, closing the high country and the main scenic roads. Hikers can use snowshoes on lower valley routes near the park entrances, passing through snow-covered forests.
months.4: Valley bottoms begin to thaw, opening a few low-elevation dirt paths near the park edges. The high country, including the Going-to-the-Sun Road, remains buried under deep snow and inaccessible to hikers.
months.7: The high country is fully accessible, opening routes like the Highline Trail. Hikers traverse steep, rocky ledges above glacier-carved valleys filled with blooming wildflowers.
months.10: The Going-to-the-Sun Road closes around the third Monday of the month, cutting off access to the high alpine trailheads. Hikers can still enjoy frosty hikes in the lower valleys before heavy snows arrive.
months.12: Deep snow blankets the parks, closing the high country and the main scenic roads. Hikers can use snowshoes on lower valley routes near the park entrances, passing through snow-covered forests.

guatemala.overview: Guatemala is known for its volcano hikes, particularly the strenuous ascents near Antigua. The overnight trek up Acatenango delivers views of neighboring Fuego erupting, while Pacaya, an active volcano, is a shorter guided climb. Trails around Lake Atitlán connect Maya villages along the steep caldera walls. The dry season from November to April brings the clearest views and safest trail conditions.

fiji.overview: Fiji has rewarding day hikes through tropical forests and along rugged shorelines. On Taveuni, the Lavena Coastal Walk leads past beaches to a waterfall, requiring a village fee and a rope-assisted creek crossing. On Viti Levu, hikers can tackle the steep trail up the 3,650-foot Mount Batilamu for sweeping island views.

jordan.overview: Hiking here means walking among ancient sandstone ruins and vast desert landscapes. At Petra, the steep climb up 800 rock-cut steps to the Monastery earns views over the valleys, while the back-door trail from Little Petra is a longer approach along the Jordan Trail. In Wadi Rum, guided desert walks explore towering rock formations and deep canyons. The best hiking is in the mild spring and fall.

gbr.overview: The islands off Queensland's coast feature real walking, reached by boat or ferry. The best-known route is the Ngaro Track in the Whitsundays, with island day hikes to viewpoints over the turquoise water. The cooler months from May to October are the only sensible time to walk, as tropical heat and humidity make the rest of the year hard going.

joshua-tree.overview: Palm Springs and Joshua Tree deliver striking desert hiking, from boulder-strewn landscapes to high alpine ridges. Hikers can explore the palm oases of Indian Canyons or take the aerial tramway to the Mount San Jacinto wilderness for high-elevation trails, where a free permit is required. The season is strictly dictated by the desert heat, making winter the prime time to explore.

jamaica.overview: Jamaica's best hiking is anchored by the Blue Mountains, where steep, forested trails lead up to the island's highest point. The classic route is the long day hike to Blue Mountain Peak, often started well before dawn to catch the sunrise and clear views stretching to the coast before the daily clouds roll in. The dry months from December to April bring the most reliable trail conditions.

istanbul.overview: Istanbul has modest but real walking escapes from the city, reached by a short drive or ferry ride. The Princes' Islands have car-free paved and dirt paths with views over the Sea of Marmara, while Belgrad Forest has shaded dirt trails under oak and beech. Spring and fall bring the best walking weather, avoiding the heavy heat of summer and the chill of winter.

ireland.overview: Ireland features excellent coastal and mountain hiking, anchored by long-distance routes like the nine-day Kerry Way and the week-long, 82-mile Wicklow Way. Day hikers can tackle the steep, rocky ascent of Carrauntoohil, the country's highest peak, or explore the rugged cliffs of the west coast. The terrain is famously green and often boggy.

greenland.overview: Greenland delivers vast, remote tundra hiking, highlighted by the 100-mile Arctic Circle Trail from Kangerlussuaq to Sisimiut. This demanding seven- to ten-day trek requires complete self-sufficiency, passing deep fjords, glacier-carved valleys and inland lakes. Day hikers can walk from coastal towns among icebergs and rugged peaks. The brief hiking window runs from June to August.

months.10: Snow begins to accumulate across the tundra, closing multi-day routes and restricting hikers to short, icy paths near the towns.

ghana.overview: Ghana features modest day hikes built around waterfalls and forest. The standout is the guided hike to the upper tier of Wli Falls, said to be West Africa's tallest waterfall, while Mount Afadjato is a short, steep climb to a summit widely regarded as the country's highest. Kakum National Park has a guided canopy walkway above the rainforest.

fjords.overview: The Norwegian Fjords feature some of the most dramatic day hiking in Europe, with trails climbing steeply from the water to sheer cliffs and panoramic ridges. Famous routes include the long, rough hike to Trolltunga, the shorter Preikestolen and Kjeragbolten, and the Besseggen ridge, a classic high-country traverse. The season is short, dictated by snow and daylight, with the high trails only reliably open from midsummer to early fall.

months.2: The high fjord trails remain buried under winter snow. Hikers are restricted to low coastal paths and groomed snowshoe routes.

faroe-islands.overview: The Faroe Islands deliver dramatic day hikes to sheer sea cliffs, deep fjords, and isolated lighthouses. Trails are mostly steep, unmarked sheep paths over rough grass, requiring hikers to navigate unpredictable Atlantic weather. Famous routes like the walk to the Kallur lighthouse or the cliff trail above Sørvágsvatn charge mandatory hiking fees. Visitors reach trailheads by rental car or ferry, with the best conditions aligning with the long daylight of mid-year.

months.2: February storms and freezing temperatures keep the high ridges and exposed sea cliffs off-limits. Hikers are restricted to short, sheltered routes near the villages during the brief daylight hours.
months.10: October brings heavy rain and low clouds, turning the steep grassy paths into slick mud. Only the most weather-hardy hikers venture onto the ridges, and many ferry-dependent routes become unreliable.

months.7: The inland valley gets genuinely scorching. Walking the exposed, steep vineyard terraces is punishing in the intense heat, pushing most hikers to stick to the breezy coastal paths near Porto.

chamonix.overview: Chamonix is famous for the multi-day Tour du Mont Blanc and high-altitude day hikes accessed by cable cars and cog railways. Trails in the Aiguilles Rouges give spectacular views across the valley to the glaciers and peaks of the Mont Blanc massif. The season is strictly dictated by snow, with high routes and lifts operating from June to mid-September.

cape-cod-islands.overview: Cape Cod and the islands have modest, easy walking on flat, sandy trails through pine barrens, salt marshes, and coastal dunes. The walking is a quiet addition to a beach trip rather than a main draw, with short nature loops and coastal paths that explore the protected shores of the Cape Cod National Seashore.

charleston-savannah.overview: Walking here means flat, easy trails through maritime forests and salt marshes. Routes at places like Skidaway Island feature boardwalks and dirt paths under Spanish moss. The best conditions are in the mild spring and fall, while summer brings intense heat and heavy humidity.

death-valley.overview: Death Valley delivers surreal desert hiking through colorful badlands, salt flats, and narrow canyons. The best hiking is concentrated in the cooler winter months, with popular day hikes like the Golden Canyon loop exploring the eroded hills. In summer, the valley floor becomes dangerously hot, pushing the only viable hiking high up to the long, strenuous climb of Telescope Peak.

chilean-lake-district.overview: The Chilean Lake District has day hikes through ancient araucaria (monkey puzzle) forests to glacier-fed lakes and volcanic craters. The signature route is the guided walk-up of the active Villarrica volcano, earning views into its smoking crater. Lower trails in Huerquehue National Park loop past waterfalls and alpine lagoons, while the region's heavy rainfall means the hiking season is strictly tied to the drier months.

colombian-andes.overview: The Colombian Andes feature striking high-altitude hiking, from the towering wax palms of the Cocora Valley to the high páramo above the cloud forest. Day hikers can explore cloud forests and unique páramo ecosystems, while multi-day treks reach remote alpine lakes and rugged summits. The best conditions align with the two drier windows from December to February and June to August.

canaries.overview: The Canary Islands deliver a massive variety of volcanic trails, from the ancient laurel forests of Tenerife and La Gomera to the deep calderas of La Palma. The standout day hike is the 12,188-foot summit of Mount Teide, reached via a steep climb or a cable car to the upper slopes, though the final push requires an advance permit. Hikers can find everything from easy coastal paths to steep ridge scrambles across the archipelago.

months.7: Midsummer heat makes exposed coastal and low-altitude trails demanding. The best hiking is found above 6,000 feet or in the dense, cloud-draped laurel forests where temperatures stay mild.
months.8: Midsummer heat makes exposed coastal and low-altitude trails demanding. The best hiking is found above 6,000 feet or in the dense, cloud-draped laurel forests where temperatures stay mild.

ethiopia.overview: Ethiopia's Simien Mountains have some of Africa's most dramatic high-altitude trekking, with sheer escarpments and deep gorges. Routes range from three-day treks along the plateau edge to expedition treks up the 14,930-foot Ras Dashen, with gelada baboons grazing beside the high trails. The national park requires an entrance permit, a guide, and a compulsory armed scout.

months.5: Rain becomes more consistent, softening the trails and bringing more cloud cover to the high peaks. Multi-day treks are still possible, but hikers will face muddy sections and obscured views on the higher passes.
months.10: The dry weather returns, opening up the high-altitude trekking routes once again. The trails dry out quickly, and hikers are rewarded with sharp, clear views over a landscape that is lush and green from the recent rains.

ecuadorian-andes.overview: The Ecuadorian Andes feature high-altitude walking among glacier-capped volcanoes, deep crater lakes, and cloud forests. Day hikers can explore the paramo grasslands of Cotopaxi National Park or the lake-dotted valleys of Cajas, while trekkers take on the multi-day Quilotoa Loop, roughly 25 miles in three days, between remote Andean villages. The trails often sit above 10,000 feet, making acclimatization essential, and the best volcano views require walking during the drier months.

months.12: A brief, unpredictable dry spell sometimes clears the skies for a few days, but hikers should generally expect wet trails and mixed visibility.

dubai.overview: Dubai's hiking is found outside the city in the rugged Hajar Mountains. The Hatta Wadi Hub has a network of marked trails through rocky valleys, while a drive to Jebel Jais in neighboring Ras Al Khaimah reaches the country's highest peak and cooler air. Walking here is strictly a winter activity, as the barren, rocky terrain is fully exposed to the intense desert sun.

cotswolds.overview: The Cotswolds feature gentle, pastoral walking through rolling hills, sheep pastures, and honey-colored stone villages. Paths follow public footpaths and bridleways across farmland and through ancient woodlands. The 102-mile Cotswold Way, usually walked in 7 to 10 days, is the main long-distance route, running along the western escarpment with views over the Severn Vale, while shorter loops connect historic market towns.

cornwall.overview: Cornwall is defined by the South West Coast Path, a continuous trail tracing the jagged shoreline; the Padstow to St Ives stretch alone is about 66 miles over six days. Hikers come for dramatic granite cliffs, hidden coves, and sweeping ocean views that can only be reached on foot. The hiking ranges from easy headland loops to steep ascents out of deep river valleys, with inland options across the rugged expanse of Bodmin Moor.

months.1: Winter brings fierce Atlantic winds, rain, and muddy trails, but the coastal path remains fully open. Hikers who brave the weather find dramatic, storm-battered cliffs and empty paths.
months.2: Fierce Atlantic winds, rain, and muddy trails define the late winter, though the coastal path remains fully open. Hikers who brave the weather find dramatic, storm-battered cliffs.
months.4: Crisp, clear days and blooming coastal flora make this a prime time for day hikes. The weather is generally stable, though hikers should still pack for sudden rain.
months.12: Winter brings fierce Atlantic winds, rain, and muddy trails, but the coastal path remains fully open. Hikers who brave the weather find dramatic, storm-battered cliffs.

chiapas.overview: Chiapas features walking through dense rainforests, highland pine forests, and around ancient Maya ruins. Trails range from short paths along the turquoise cascades of El Chiflón and the lakes of Montebello to deeper day hikes into the Lacandon Jungle, taken with a local guide. The dry months from November to April provide the best conditions, avoiding the heavy mud and intense humidity of the summer wet season.

edinburgh.overview: Edinburgh features surprisingly good walking right on its doorstep. The obvious draw is Arthur's Seat, an extinct volcano rising above the city that provides a short, steep hike to panoramic views. Just south of town, the Pentland Hills Regional Park has miles of rolling ridges and reservoir loops for longer day hikes.

denali-interior.overview: Denali features a mix of marked trails near the park entrance and vast, trail-less tundra for off-trail hiking. Day hikers can tackle the steep Mount Healy Overlook for views of the Alaska Range or walk the easier Savage River Loop. Beyond mile 15, park buses drop hikers directly into the wilderness to navigate the open tundra and braided river valleys on their own.

copenhagen.overview: Copenhagen has easy, flat walking rather than true hiking. The best trails are just outside the city in Jægersborg Dyrehave, a former royal hunting ground with ancient oak trees, or the coastal paths of Naturpark Amager.

buenosaires.overview: Walking here means flat nature paths and park strolls rather than mountain hiking. The Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur features miles of dirt paths through wetlands on the Río de la Plata, while Tigre has short trails along the delta waterways an hour north.

belize.overview: Belize features tropical forest trails leading to hidden waterfalls and sweeping jungle canopy views. The best day hikes are in the Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary, a jaguar reserve where the Tiger Fern Trail climbs to a double waterfall, and at Mayflower Bocawina National Park, where a rope-assisted climb ends at Antelope Falls and its pools. The dry months provide the most reliable footing, as heavy rains quickly turn the clay trails slick.

cape-town.overview: Table Mountain and the Cape Peninsula deliver outstanding day hikes right above the city, from easy coastal and fynbos paths around Cape Point to steep scrambles up the mountain's sandstone cliffs. The hiking is best from March to May and from September to November, when the weather is mild.

berlin.overview: Berlin is a flat city, but the forests and lakes on its edges have easy, shaded walking. The Grunewald forest and the paths along the Havel river provide miles of wide trails under the trees, reachable by train.

badlands-black-hills.overview: The region features two distinct landscapes for day hikers: the exposed, eroded pinnacles of the Badlands and the shaded ponderosa pine forests of the Black Hills. Trails range from easy prairie loops to the climb up Black Elk Peak, which rewards hikers with views of granite spires. The 111-mile Centennial Trail provides a multi-day trek through the hills and plains. Spring and autumn bring the most reliable weather across both areas.

borabora.overview: French Polynesia delivers rugged, steep jungle trails leading to volcanic viewpoints, though the network is modest. On Bora Bora, the steep scramble up Mount Pahia requires a guide, while the shoulder of Mount Otemanu has a challenging day hike beneath the sheer summit cliffs. The best hiking is found from May to October when the paths are drier and less slippery.

bavaria-munich.overview: The real hiking is about an hour and a half south of the city in the Bavarian Alps, where trains and cable cars lift hikers to high ridge trails above alpine lakes. The network around Garmisch and Mittenwald features everything from easy valley loops to rugged limestone summits and multi-day hut-to-hut routes.

black-forest.overview: The Black Forest delivers a vast network of trails through dense conifers, open pastures, and deep gorges, with cable cars lifting hikers to the higher ridges. The Westweg is a famous 177-mile trek running the length of the region in about two weeks. Day hikes range from easy lakeside paths to climbs up the Feldberg, the highest peak.

months.6: The best hiking of the year, with all trails and huts open for the Westweg trek and day hikes to the Feldberg summit.
months.7: The best hiking of the year, with all trails and huts open for the Westweg trek and day hikes to the Feldberg summit.
months.8: The best hiking of the year, with all trails and huts open for the Westweg trek and day hikes to the Feldberg summit.

bhutan.overview: Bhutan has some of the most dramatic and remote hiking in the Himalayas, from steep forest day hikes to legendary high-altitude expedition treks. The steep climb to the cliffside Tiger's Nest monastery is the best known day hike, while the multi-week Snowman Trek and the shorter Druk Path Trek cross remote passes beneath unclimbed peaks. All hiking requires a licensed guide and a daily fee, keeping the trails pristine. The best hiking is in spring and autumn.

belfast-giants-causeway.overview: The coastal cliffs and heather-covered granite peaks feature strong regional hiking, anchored by the Causeway Coast Way, a 33-mile trek over two to three days past basalt columns and ruined castles. Day hikers head to the Mourne Mountains for steep climbs up Slieve Donard, or the Glens of Antrim for forest and waterfall loops.

months.3: Daylight lengthens and the mountain trails begin to dry out, though the high granite peaks remain cold and windy. The coastal trek becomes more reliable for multi-day hikers.
months.11: Shortening daylight and frequent storms leave the high peaks heavily exposed. Hikers stick to the lower coastal paths and sheltered glens, which stay open year-round.

beijing.overview: The hiking here is defined by the Great Wall, offering routes along ancient stone paths and crumbling watchtowers that trace the mountain ridges. Visitors typically take a shuttle or cable car to reach restored sections like Mutianyu and Jinshanling for day hikes, while wild stretches like Jiankou give steep scrambling over crumbling wall. The best hiking is in spring and autumn when the air is clear and temperatures are mild.

months.12: Freezing temperatures and strong winds return to the mountains. The steep stone steps are bitterly cold, though the restored sections remain open for hardy hikers. Winter heating-season smog often leaves the air poor.

amalfi.overview: The steep cliffs and terraced hillsides above the Mediterranean deliver excellent day hikes, led by the famous Path of the Gods. This route follows the high ridges between Bomerano and Nocelle, delivering sweeping views of the coastline and the sea. Other trails explore deep gorges like the Valle delle Ferriere, passing waterfalls and ruins. Most trailheads are reached by local bus or by hiking up from the coastal towns.

bend-crater-lake.overview: The volcanic landscapes of Central Oregon have routes ranging from loops along the deep blue waters of Crater Lake to challenging ascents in the high Cascades. Hikers can explore easy paths along the Deschutes River near Bend or tackle the strenuous climb up South Sister for panoramic views of glaciers and cinder cones. Central Cascades wilderness permits are required for many of the best high-elevation mountain routes from mid-June to mid-October.

months.1: Deep snow covers the high Cascades and Crater Lake, closing the mountain routes. Hikers can use snowshoes on the unplowed sections of the Rim Drive and groomed winter trails near Bend.
months.2: Deep snow covers the high Cascades and Crater Lake, closing the mountain routes. Hikers can use snowshoes on the unplowed sections of the Rim Drive and groomed winter trails near Bend.
months.3: Deep snow covers the high Cascades and Crater Lake, closing the mountain routes. Hikers can use snowshoes on the unplowed sections of the Rim Drive and groomed winter trails near Bend.
months.11: Heavy snow accumulates in the mountains, closing the Crater Lake rim and high Cascade trails to hikers. Only the lowest valley paths remain clear.
months.12: Deep snow covers the high Cascades and Crater Lake, closing the mountain routes. Hikers can use snowshoes on the unplowed sections of the Rim Drive and groomed winter trails near Bend.

months.1: The Park Loop Road is closed to cars and trails are often covered in ice or snow. Hikers stick to the carriage roads for easy snowshoeing, while the steep mountain trails are treacherous.

angkor.overview: Cambodia features jungle treks and waterfall day hikes, mostly in the Cardamom Mountains, Virachey National Park, and the hills of Mondulkiri. Routes range from day hikes to multi-day jungle treks that require a local guide. The dry months from November to February bring the best conditions, while heavy rains later in the year turn trails into deep mud.

months.9: The wettest part of the year keeps jungle paths muddy and river crossings high, limiting hikers to easy local paths.

andalucia.overview: Hiking ranges from the high peaks of the Sierra Nevada to deep limestone gorges. The famous Caminito del Rey is a point to point hike including sections of suspended boardwalk pinned to the sheer walls of the Gaitanes Gorge. This walk requires a timed ticket, and most visitors take a shuttle to the start. The high mountains deliver strenuous day hikes to summits like Mulhacén. The hiking is best in spring and autumn, as summer heat is extreme.

months.12: Winter walking is mild and generally sunny, though hikers should expect occasional rain showers. The coastal paths remain fully accessible.

months.1: The northeast monsoon brings heavy rain and muddy trails to the rainforest. The Mount Kinabalu summit climb can be closed at short notice by dangerous weather, making this a tough time for hikers.

months.11: Heavy rain and low visibility make the high routes like Mount Pico slippery and unrewarding. Hikers stick to the sheltered laurel forests and coastal paths, which stay walkable despite the wet conditions.

atacama.overview: The high-altitude desert has stark, otherworldly day hikes through slot canyons and jagged rock formations. The best-known routes explore the Valle de la Luna, where trails wind past sand dunes and salt-crusted cliffs, and the Guatin Canyon, known for its giant cacti. Tickets for popular areas must be bought in advance if not hiking as part of a guided itinerary.

athens.overview: The mountains ringing the city feature day hikes a short drive from the center. Mount Parnitha, the highest, has trails through pine forests to mountain refuges, while Mount Hymettus has rocky, exposed routes with views over the capital and the Saronic Gulf. Spring and autumn are best, as summer brings dangerous heat and fire-risk trail closures.

big-island.overview: The Big Island delivers a unique mix of volcanic landscapes and coastal trails, from the stark lava fields of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park to the lush valleys of the north coast. The steep hike down into Waipi'o Valley or the trails around Kilauea's caldera show off scenery that can only be reached on foot. The dry season from May to September is the most reliable time to walk, especially on the rainier eastern side.

months.12: Winter rains are frequent on the windward side, often clouding the views in the national park. The best hiking is found on the dry, sunny Kona coast.

barbados.overview: Barbados features modest walking along its rugged east coast and inland gullies. The best route is the coastal path from Bath to Bathsheba, passing Atlantic surf and limestone formations. Inland, short easy walks explore forest patches. Best from December to April.

aspen.overview: The Elk Mountains feature high-altitude trails past alpine lakes and jagged peaks, with the best views reached by a mandatory shuttle to the Maroon Bells trailhead. Day hikes range from easy valley loops to steep climbs, while the Four Pass Loop is a strenuous 26-mile trek over four days. The best-known trails are crowded in summer, requiring timed reservations for the shuttle and parking. The main hiking season runs from July to September when the high passes are clear of snow.

months.4: Snow begins to melt, leaving the lower valley paths muddy and icy, while the high routes remain deep in snow and inaccessible to hikers.
months.5: Lower trails clear of snow and offer day hikes, but the high passes and multi-day treks remain snowbound and closed to hikers.

torres-del-paine.overview: Granite towers, glaciers and turquoise lakes surround the trails here. Day hikes start from trailheads reached by bus or catamaran, while the famous W Trek (about 40 miles in 4 to 6 days) and O Circuit (about 80 miles in 7 to 9 days) give long multi-day routes between refugios. The weather is notoriously windy, and the main trekking window runs from October to April when the trails and huts are fully open.

months.6: The trails are largely snowbound and the multi-day treks are closed to independent hikers. Only a few low-elevation paths remain open for short day hikes.

months.12: The trails are buried under winter snow, with high avalanche risk on the slopes, restricting hikers to the easy groomed paths and snowshoe routes in the valley bottoms.

tokyo-kyoto.overview: The forested mountains surrounding both cities deliver excellent day hikes reached easily by train, often with a cable car or chairlift to bypass the steepest climbs. Trails link ancient shrines and cedar groves, like the ridge path from Kurama to Kibune in Kyoto or the routes up Mount Takao and Mount Mitake outside Tokyo. Clear days on the Tokyo trails earn distant views of Mount Fuji.

months.1: Winter brings more rain and cloud to the high peaks, making the ridge routes slippery and less rewarding. The lower levada paths stay green, though hikers should expect occasional showers.
months.2: Winter brings more rain and cloud to the high peaks, making the ridge routes slippery and less rewarding. The lower levada paths stay green, though hikers should expect occasional showers.
months.12: Winter brings more rain and cloud to the high peaks, making the ridge routes slippery and less rewarding. The lower levada paths stay green, though hikers should expect occasional showers.

chicago.overview: The best hiking lies about an hour outside the city, where the trails of Indiana Dunes National Park cross wooded dunes to the lake. Closer in, the Palos Trail System has loops through forest preserves.

arches-canyonlands.overview: The hiking here explores two distinct desert landscapes: the concentrated sandstone fins and windows of Arches, and the vast, deep gorges of Canyonlands. Most routes are day hikes across bare slickrock, leading to iconic formations like Delicate Arch or the canyon rims at Island in the Sky. The Needles district features longer, rugged day hikes and multi-day routes through colorful sandstone spires. The labyrinth of the Fiery Furnace requires a specific permit to enter.

months.1: Winter brings freezing temperatures and occasional snow, which makes the slickrock trails icy and slow. The main paths remain open for prepared hikers.

aruba.overview: The arid scrub and rugged windward coast of Arikok National Park have modest but scenic walking. Trails range from easy coastal paths to a climb up Mount Jamanota, the island's highest point, earning views of the Caribbean. The climate is hot year-round, so hikers start at dawn to beat the midday sun.

basque-country.overview: The Basque coast and green interior have excellent day hikes, from the dramatic flysch cliffs between Zumaia and Deba to the steep climb up to the hermitage at San Juan de Gaztelugatxe. Inland, the trails of Gorbea Natural Park cross lush forests and open ridges.
